general_questions: What is your minimum size, and what would it cost at $5M: setup and legal costs, annual management fee, any per-loan charges? Who pays them?
Can you accept grants, recoverable grants and loans into the same vehicle? If not, what structure do you suggest for the loans?
Can you lend to funds and borrowers outside the US? Any country or currency limits?
Do you have experience with subordinated debt?
Who sits on the credit committee, and what formal role can AEF have?
How deep is your underwriting, and can a separate advisor do it instead?

Can the vehicle grow later or be spun out? Could its loans be moved into a larger fund later (warehousing), and what would that need: lender consent, a valuation method, and how DAF capital is treated?
What else are you doing that is similar (other vehicles, funds or programs)? Would any of them compete with this vehicle for deals or attention?
What experience do you have with agriculture, agroecology, and lending to funds rather than directly to companies?
How would this advance your mission, and why would you take on a ~$5M mandate? What would you gain beyond fees?

organizations.lends_internationally_note: via DAF investments, e.g. an emerging-markets credit strategy
organizations.underwriting: Client (AEF or its advisor) for client-recommended investments; ImpactAssets does a compliance-level review
organizations.summary: The DAF lets donors recommend impact investments in funds and companies as well as grants. It supports international grants and expenditure responsibility grants. Several services appear to be open to non-DAF clients: a PRI account for foundations, Pooled Donor Funds, Supporting Organizations ($10M+ accounts), custom portfolios, due diligence and back-office administration. The DAF can make loans through the Client Recommended Investment service, with ImpactAssets handling execution, servicing, monitoring and reporting. For client-recommended investments, the client sources the deal and does the due diligence; ImpactAssets reviews impact commitments, runs basic AML, IRS-compliance and fraud checks, acts as legal investor and fiduciary, and can decline. An emerging-markets credit strategy is available through the DAF.

organizations.name: Innpact
organizations.type: Impact fund structuring firm and third-party AIFM (Luxembourg)
organizations.size_note: Luxembourg regulated structure likely too heavy for ~$5M (per AEF / to confirm).

organizations.summary: Luxembourg impact finance firm that sets up and manages impact funds (S29). Services include fund strategy and structuring; a third-party AIFM dedicated to impact funds, supporting RAIF and SIF vehicles and blended finance structures (S29); a Mauritius fund-management route for African funds through MIFGA, a joint initiative with AXIS (S29); and a white-label impact bond issuance platform, Imagine Impact Bonds (S29). Design only: Innpact supported IDH in the design, structuring and incorporation of the EUR 100 million IDH Farmfit Fund (Farmfit Fund B.V., Netherlands, January 2020) (S31); the fund is managed by IDH Investment Management (S32). AIFM: Innpact Fund Management S.A. has been AIFM of the Agri-Business Capital (ABC) Fund, a Luxembourg private debt fund, since 2023 (S30), and still listed it among its funds under management on 30 June 2026 (S33). See the ABC Fund example. Innpact's site gives no fund sizes or minimums (S29).

examples.name: Olamina Fund
examples.label: Closest structure
examples.structure: Olamina Fund, LLC, offered to accredited investors under Rule 506(c). Investors choose a 5-year note at a fixed 1% a year or a 7-year note at a fixed 1.5%. The initial $40M came from two of Candide's donor-advised fund clients; ImpactAssets made the initial investments, advised by members of the Pritzker family. It makes senior unsecured loans of up to $4M to CDFIs and other loan funds, plus smaller direct loans, with at least 80% of loans going to organizations led by people of color and women. The credit committee is the Managing Director and Candide's two founding partners, and a Community Advisory Board has a veto over every loan.
examples.why_relevant: A note-issuing vehicle run by an investment manager, with a DAF as one of its investors. This gets around the fact that a DAF can't accept loans: an AEF DAF could invest in such a vehicle alongside other lenders. The community veto mirrors AEF's participatory governance.
examples.key_differences: US only (rural areas, Native lands and the deep South). Its initial $40M is eight times the pilot.

examples.name: Buen Vivir Fund
examples.label: Lessons learned
examples.run_by: Thousand Currents, which hosted the fund and was both its funder and facilitator. Closed in 2023.
examples.structure: A participatory fund whose members included grassroots groups from Mexico, Guatemala, India, Nepal and South Africa, along with US philanthropies. It made six loans across three countries between 2018 and 2020, each paired with grant support. Instead of interest, borrowers made "aportes", solidarity contributions above the return of principal. A Members Assembly, not an investment committee, governed the fund.
examples.why_relevant: The closest precedent in mission, geography and governance.
examples.what_happened: Pandemic-era unrestricted grants strained its financial model, and by late 2022 only one member could make an aporte. In 2023 Thousand Currents ended all programmatic investment, and all outstanding loans were converted into grants.
examples.lessons: Regulatory compliance is difficult and expensive for small funds; participation doesn't remove power dynamics, especially when the host is also the funder; not all work suits loans; and responsibility should match readiness.

sources.label: Nonprofit Quarterly, Buen Vivir Fund (May 28, 2025)

examples.name: ABC Fund (Agri-Business Capital Fund)
examples.label: Regulated manager with a separate investment advisor
examples.structure: Luxembourg SA, SICAV-RAIF launched in February 2019 (S30), originally sponsored by IFAD (S34). Invests in private debt with a global mandate focused on Sub-Saharan Africa; end-beneficiaries are smallholder farmers and local communities (S30). Innpact Fund Management S.A. was selected as AIFM in 2022 and appointed toward the end of Q1 2023 (S30). ABC was originally managed by Bamboo Capital Partners (S34, S35), with Injaro Investments as investment advisor (S34). Innpact's website currently lists Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P) as investment advisor (S30). In 2020 the fund had a target size of €200 million and had investors including IFAD (with funds from the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation), the European Commission, the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States, Luxembourg and AGRA (S35).
examples.why_relevant: Separates the regulated fund manager from the party advising on investments — close to the AIF model, where AEF takes part in decisions and a third party underwrites. Lends to agriculture in Sub-Saharan Africa and is structured to blend public with private capital (S35).
examples.key_differences: Much larger (€200 million 2020 target vs. a ~$5M pilot). A Luxembourg regulated fund with public and institutional investors; accepting US grants or recoverable grants is not described. No participatory governance described.

examples.name: MCE Social Capital
examples.label: Philanthropic guarantees backing international loans
examples.structure: High-net-worth individuals and foundations (Guarantors) sign philanthropic guarantee agreements. MCE uses their credit to borrow from US and European financial institutions and accredited investors, and lends to financial service providers and small and growing businesses in emerging markets (S38). Guarantors don't move assets upfront; if a loan defaults, the relevant Guarantors share the loss pro rata through tax-deductible contributions. Capital recycles as loans are repaid (S38). As of June 30, 2026, more than 100 Guarantors had provided $85.5 million in guarantees (S38). MCE also runs the MESA Fund for smallholder resilience and women in agriculture (S38).
examples.why_relevant: A different inflow from anything else on this page: donors back loans with guarantees instead of giving or lending cash, and the vehicle borrows against them. It lends internationally, including to agriculture, and recycles capital.
examples.key_differences: Lends directly to financial service providers and businesses, not to funds. Much larger than the pilot. A guarantee layer needs a lender willing to borrow against it, which adds a party to the structure.
